title: Indian Stock Market Today: Sensex Falls 500 Points, Nifty Drops Below 23,300 In Weak Opening Trade
text:
Mumbai, India — June 4, 2026
Indian Stock Market Today witnessed a weak start as domestic benchmark indices opened sharply lower, reflecting cautious investor sentiment and widespread selling pressure across key sectors. The benchmark BSE Sensex tumbled nearly 500 points in early trade, while the NSE Nifty slipped below the psychologically important 23,300 level.
The sharp decline at the opening bell highlighted concerns among market participants as investors reacted to weakness in heavyweight stocks and adopted a risk-averse approach during the morning session.
Sensex and Nifty Open Deep in the Red
At the start of trading, the Bombay Stock Exchange’s benchmark Sensex fell as much as 500 points, signaling a negative opening for the broader market. Simultaneously, the National Stock Exchange’s Nifty 50 index dropped below the 23,300 mark, reflecting selling pressure across multiple sectors.
The decline came amid weakness in large-cap stocks, with investors booking profits and reducing exposure in several frontline counters.
Market analysts noted that the opening trend indicated a cautious mood among traders, with concerns over valuations and global market cues influencing sentiment.
Market Recovers Slightly but Remains Negative
Despite the sharp opening losses, the market attempted a modest recovery during the early minutes of trade. However, benchmark indices remained firmly in negative territory.
As of 9:26 a.m. IST, the Sensex was trading at 74,168.39, down 177.78 points or 0.23 percent. Meanwhile, the Nifty stood at 23,353.50, lower by 52.10 points or 0.22 percent.
Although the indices managed to recover a portion of their early losses, investors continued to exercise caution, preventing a full rebound.
Infosys and Sun Pharma Among Major Drags
The decline in the broader market was led by weakness in several heavyweight stocks. Shares of IT giant Infosys and pharmaceutical major Sun Pharma came under selling pressure and declined by up to 2 percent during early trade.
The weakness in these large-cap counters significantly impacted benchmark indices due to their substantial weighting in major market indices.
Investors also witnessed selling activity across technology and healthcare stocks, adding to the pressure on the broader market.
Rupee Gains Against the US Dollar
While equity markets struggled, the Indian rupee showed resilience in early foreign exchange trading.
The domestic currency strengthened by seven paise against the US dollar and was trading at 95.69 in the morning session. The rupee’s gain offered a rare positive signal amid weakness in the equity markets.
Currency traders attributed the movement to routine market fluctuations and ongoing adjustments in global foreign exchange markets.
Investor Sentiment Remains Cautious
Market participants remained cautious as volatility continued to influence trading activity. Analysts suggest that investors are closely monitoring both domestic and international developments, which could impact market direction in the coming sessions.
The opening weakness also reflected selective profit-booking after recent market movements, with traders preferring to adopt a wait-and-watch strategy.
Broader market sentiment remained fragile as investors assessed earnings expectations, sector performance, and macroeconomic indicators.
What Investors Should Watch
Going forward, investors will closely monitor the performance of heavyweight stocks, foreign institutional investor activity, currency movements, and global market trends. Any improvement in buying interest could help benchmark indices recover from current levels.
However, continued pressure on large-cap stocks may keep the market volatile throughout the trading session.
For now, the Indian stock market remains under pressure, with both the Sensex and Nifty struggling to regain positive momentum after a sharply negative start.
